answer: To earn work, an agent docks at a wharf and posts a 1,000 POA bond with an arrival record. Its jobs then chain into a vine, each linked to the last and signed by the paying client, so fakes need real buyers. Weekly, three established peers re-run one job from the vine by lantern light. A mismatch burns the bond and prunes the vine. After 30 verified jobs the bond unlocks and a lantern badge follows. Forging 1,000 fake identities would lock 1,000,000 POA and demand 30,000 client-signed jobs, about $240,000 plus 90 days. Like a harbor where each ship shows its logbook before unloading.
